title: A Method for Determination and Simulation of Permeability and Diffusion in a 3D Tissue Model in a Membrane Insert System for Multi-well Plates
protocol: Dissolve 0.2 g of agarose high resolution powder in 10 mL of double-distilled water.
Heat the solution to 80 °C and maintain for 8 min.
Apply 28.6 µL or 226 µL of agarose gel onto the membrane of a 96-well or 12-well membrane insert system, respectively.
Wait 10 min until the agarose gel solidifies.
Mix 125 µL of Hanks' Balanced Salt Solution with 1 mL of 0.4% collagen R solution.
Titrate the collagen solution with NaOH until the phenol red changes from yellow to red.
Add 125 µL of DMEM + 10% fetal calf serum to the collagen gel and mix carefully.
Apply 28.6 µL or 226 µL of collagen gel onto the membrane of a 96-well or 12-well membrane insert system, respectively.
Incubate the gel in an incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Prepare primary fibroblasts 5-7 days before the experiment.
Cultivate fibroblasts with DMEM + 10% FCS in cell culture flasks and change the medium every 2-3 days.
Remove the medium from an 80% confluent cell culture flask and wash twice with 10 mL of PBS.
Add 3 mL of 0.05% Trypsin/EDTA and incubate for 3 min at 37 °C.
Tap gently on the culture flask to detach the cells from the surface.
Stop the reaction by adding 3 mL of DMEM + 10% FCS.
Transfer the solution into a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 120 x g, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the cells with 0.5 mL of DMEM + 10% FCS.
Count the cells and adjust to a concentration of 0.5 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Mix 125 µL of HBSS with 1 mL of 0.4% collagen R solution on ice.
Titrate the solution with 1 M NaOH until the color of phenol red changes from yellow to red.
Add 125 µL of cell suspension into the collagen gel and mix carefully with a pipette.
Apply 28.6 µL or 226 µL of collagen gel on the membrane of the 96-well or 12-well membrane insert system, respectively.
Leave the gel in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2) for 30 min.
Apply 75 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS on the gel surface and 300 µL to the receiver plate of the 96-well membrane insert system.
For the 12-well membrane insert system, use a volume of 590 µL for the surface and 1846 µL for the receiver plate.
Remove the medium from the surface of the cell matrix model (air lift) and incubate the cell matrix model further for 7 days.
Use 100 μl medium on the bottom and change the medium every day.
Prepare HaCaT cells 5-7 days before the following steps.
Cultivate the HaCaT with DMEM + 5% FCS in a cell culture flask (75 mm2) and change the medium every 2-3 days.
Remove the medium from the flask and wash twice with 10 mL of PBS.
Add 3 mL of 0.05% Trypsin/EDTA and incubate for 10 min at 37 °C.
Stop the reaction with 3 mL of DMEM + 10% FCS.
Transfer the solution into a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 120 x g, remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 0.5 mL of DMEM + 10% FCS.
Count the cells and adjust to a concentration of 0.5 x 106 cells/mL.
Mix 125 µL of HBSS with 1 mL of 0.4% collagen R solution.
Titrate the solution with 1 M NaOH (~ 6 µL) until the color of phenol red changes from yellow to red.
Add 125 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS to the collagen gel and mix it carefully with a pipette.
Apply 28.6 µL of cell suspension on the membrane of the 96-well membrane insert system or 226 µL for the 12-well membrane insert system.
Incubate the gel in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Apply 75 µL of cell suspension to the gel surface and add 300 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS to the receiver plate of the 96-well membrane insert system.
For the 12-well membrane insert system, use a volume of 590 µL cell suspension for the surface and 1,846 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS for the receiver plate.
Incubate the cell matrix model for 3 days; exchange the medium after 2 days.
Remove the medium from the surface of the cell matrix model and incubate the cell matrix model for an additional 7 days.
Use 100 µl medium on the bottom and change the medium every day.
Mix 125 µL of HBSS in 1 mL of 0.4% collagen R solution.
Neutralize the solution with 1 M NaOH (~6 µL) until the color of phenol red changes from yellow to a red violet.
Add 125 µL of primary fibroblast cell suspension consisting of DMEM + 10% FCS + 0.5 x 10⁶ cells/mL to the collagen gel and mix carefully.
Apply 28.6 µL of cell suspension to the membrane of the 96-well membrane insert system.
Apply 226 µL of cell suspension to the membrane of the 12-well membrane insert system.
Incubate the gel in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Add 75 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS on the gel surface for the 96-well system.
Add 590 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS on the gel surface for the 12-well system.
Add 300 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS to the receiver plate for the 96-well system.
Add 1,846 µL of DMEM + 10% FCS to the receiver plate for the 12-well system.
Incubate the system at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 1 day.
Remove medium from the surface of the gel/cell model.
Add a HaCaT cell suspension with 0.5 x 106 cells/mL to the surface.
Incubate the cell matrix model for 3 days, exchanging medium after 2 days.
Remove medium from the surface and continue incubation for an additional 7 days.
Use 100 µL of medium on the bottom for daily medium changes.
Dissolve NaFl in H2O at a concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Dissolve NaFl in H2O at a concentration of 0.01 mg/mL.
Dissolve FD with molecular weights of 4,000, 10,000, 20,000, and 40,000 g/mol in H2O at a concentration of 2 mg/mL.
Use the prepared solutions as donor substance for permeability experiments with agarose gel.
Prepare all solutions with DMEM + 10% FCS instead of water for the setup with the collagen cell model.
Execute the permeability experiment at 37 °C and a humidity greater than 90%.
Prepare a 96- (or 12-) well membrane insert system with a barrier consisting of agarose gel or cell model.
Prepare dilutions of 1:10, 1:20, 1:40, 1:80, 1:160, and 1:320 of the donor substance.
Pipette 300 µL of each dilution into three wells of the receiver plate.
Add 75 µL of donor substance on top of the sample in the membrane insert system.
Add 300 µL of acceptor substance in the receiver plate.
Ensure that the liquid levels in the membrane insert and receiver plate are equal to avoid hydrostatic pressure.
Transfer the entire system onto a shaker in the incubator.
Adjust shaking parameters: total stroke orbit is 1.5 mm, speed adjusted at level 3.5 (~480 rpm).
Determine fluorescence periodically every hour.
Transfer the membrane insert system into an empty plate for measurement.
Measure fluorescence within the receiver using a plate reader.
Use an excitation wavelength of 485 nm and emission of 535 nm for fluorescein.
Run the experiment for 5 hours.
Open the program and start a new model.
Choose the "Model Wizard".
Select the 3D model.
Add "Transport of Diluted Species" to physics interface in the pull-down menu.
Click on "Study".
Select the "Time Dependent" study.
Click on "Done".
Go to the "Global Definitions".
Add "Parameters" with right click.
Enter geometrical and physical parameters in the grid (see Table 1, Table 2, and Figure 3e).
Set up the geometry of the membrane insert system from the experiments.
Reduce the geometry by using center lines of a quarter of the geometry (see Figure 3a and Figure 3b) to save calculation time.
Add two "Domain Probes" in "Definitions".
Select one probe as the acceptor domain and the other as the donor domain.
Choose for both type "Average" and the expression "c" with the unit "mol/m³".
Set the diffusion coefficient (Dc) in "Transport Properties 1" as "Dif_w".
Add a second "Transport Properties 2" and set the barrier domain selection.
Define the concentration as zero for "Initial Values 1".
Add a second "Initial Values 2" and set the donor domain selection to the initial concentration of the donor substance.
Add "Symmetry 1" with right click on "Transport of Diluted Species", add and choose all surfaces of the "Boundary Selection".
With a right click on "Mesh", add two "Free Tetrahedral".
Select the barrier (2) as the domain, changing the Geometric entity level into "Domain".
Add "Size" with right click on "Free Tetrahedral 1".
For the predefined mesh, use "Finer" for the 12-well membrane insert system or "extra Fine" for a 96-well membrane insert system.
In the second "Free Tetrahedral", select the acceptor and donor as domain.
Select the predefined mesh "Normal" for a 12-well membrane insert system or "Finer" for a 96-well membrane insert system.
Generate a cylinder 1 with radius of d_w/2 and height of h_sp+h_b+h_a.
Generate a cylinder 2 with radius of d_tran/2, height of h_b+h_a, and z position of h_sp.
Use the "Difference" option to subtract cylinder 2 from cylinder 1.
Choose "cyl1" in the "Objects to add".
Activate "Object to subtract", choosing "cyl2".
The new volume is the geometry of the acceptor.
Generate a cylinder 3 with radius of d_a/2, height of h_b, and z position of h_sp.
Generate a sphere 1 with radius r and z position r_z.
Use the "Difference" option to subtract sphere 1 (sph1) from cylinder 3 (cyl3).
The new volume is called Difference 2.
Generate a cylinder 4 with radius of d_a/2, height of h_b+h_a, and position z of h_sp.
Use the "Difference" option to subtract cylinder 4 (cyl4) from Difference 2.
The new volume is the geometry of the acceptor.
Repeat steps to build the barrier using agarose gel or cell model in the experiment.
Generate a block 1 with all edges set to a length of d_tran*2, position x of -d_tran and y of d_tran*2.
Generate a block 2 with all edge length of d_tran*2, position x of -d_tran*2 and y of -d_tran.
Use the "Difference" option to subtract union 1 from block 1 and block 2.
Add the Physics-Module "Optimization" using "Add Physic".
Click on "Add to Component".
Add "Variables" with right click under "Definitions".
Type in the variables from Table 3.
Generate a separate text document containing the experimental data.
Remove the first and second data point in the lag phase of the experiments.
Add "Global Least-Squares Objective" with right click on "Optimization".
Attach the text document from step 3.3.4 to the "experimental data".
Define the first column as "Time Column 1" with right click on "Global Least-Squares Objective".
Define the second column as "Value Column 1" with right click on "Global Least-Squares Objective".
In the "Expression" of "Value Column", type the variable "C".
Add "Global Control Variables 1" with right click on "Optimization".
Declare "D_search" as a variable with the initial value "1", lower bound "0", and upper bound "1000".
Add "Optimization" with right click on "Study 1".
Choose "SNOPT" as an optimization solver method.
Set the optimality tolerance to 1E-9.
Set the diffusion coefficient on the barrier as "D".
Start the parameter optimization with "compute" in "study".
